title: Khagemba Coins and Brick Bridges
subtitle: How a Frontier King Forged Bridges, Coin and a New People in Manipur
region: Kangla, Khwairamband, Cachar and the northern frontier
moral: Wisdom can turn danger at the border into tools for the realm.

sources.citation: Parratt, The Court Chronicle of the Kings of Manipur, Vol. 1 (2005)
sources.note: Khagemba entries for battles, settlers, rules and court institutions.

sources.citation: Kangla gate, Khwairamband bridge traditions and Khagemba-era coins in Manipur collections
sources.note: Material witnesses for brick-building and monetization, though many structures are restored.

sources.citation: Shobhana L. Chelliah, 'Asserting Nationhood through Personal Name Choice', Anthropological Linguistics 47(2), 2005
sources.note: Recent study useful for Khagemba's name, identity and Meitei social memory.

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Kangla citadel with brick gate and distant bridge over a river, King Senbi Khagemba silhouetted in foreground

dialogue.text: In the hills of Manipur, King Senbi Khagemba turned defeated foes into settlers, war captives into builders, and a land of barter into one of bridges and coin.

panels.shot: tight medium on Khagemba in armour, map of eastern frontier and hills behind him

dialogue.text: When Senbi Khagemba took the throne around 1597, Manipur was ringed by restless frontiers—hill chiefs, Cachar plains, and distant forces pressing at every path.

panels.shot: wide battlefield shot, distant opposing force on a plain beyond a river, Khagemba’s troops in foreground

dialogue.text: The court chronicle speaks of many clashes—north and west, towards Cachar and the hills—where Khagemba met raiding forces in open field and narrow passes.

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over a battlefield after combat, lines of disarmed captives surrounded by Manipuri soldiers

dialogue.text: Among the captured were Muslim soldiers from the western frontiers, men the chronicle remembers as the seed of the Meitei Pangal community.

panels.shot: medium shot of Khagemba dismounted, regarding a group of captives of varied appearance

dialogue.speaker: king_senbi_khagemba
dialogue.text: You came as enemies. Will you stay as people of this valley?

panels.shot: wide shot of a valley settlement being laid out, with Khagemba pointing as captives and locals build together

dialogue.text: Instead of scattering them, Khagemba settled these Muslims in the valley, under his protection, binding them by land, duty and marriage to the kingdom.

panels.shot: intimate medium inside a house, a Meitei elder and a Muslim settler sharing food as Khagemba is glimpsed outside

dialogue.text: Over time they became the Meitei Pangals, their descendants still part of Manipuri life—a frontier defeat turned into a new people within the kingdom.

panels.shot: sweeping wide of Nambul river with workers building a brick bridge under supervision

dialogue.text: The chronicle and local tradition remember Khagemba’s reign for bridges and brick—new ways to bind the capital to its markets and the hills beyond.

panels.shot: medium on masons laying bricks for an arch, Khagemba in background; suggestion of foreign technique but no labels

dialogue.text: Stories speak of captured builders who brought new brick techniques to Kangla’s gate and the river bridge, though outside records have yet to echo their names.

panels.shot: majestic low-angle of the completed brick gate of Kangla with Khagemba passing beneath

dialogue.text: Whatever its precise origin, the brick arch at Kangla became a sign: stone and clay now stood where earlier wood and thatch had guarded the palace.

panels.shot: busy market wide shot at Khwairamband, with bridge in background and diverse traders

dialogue.text: With bridges came markets—Khwairamband and others—drawing hill produce, valley rice, and distant goods into one restless river of trade.

panels.shot: close-up on hands exchanging small silverish coins in the market

dialogue.text: Archaeologists today still find coins of Khagemba’s time—metal stamped with royal authority, easing trade where once only barter fixed the price of salt and rice.

panels.shot: medium shot inside a mint-like workshop, artisans striking coins under Khagemba’s supervision

dialogue.speaker: king_senbi_khagemba
dialogue.text: Let this mark carry Kangla’s word to every hand in the valley.

panels.shot: dynamic medium shot of Sagol Kangjei game on open field, Khagemba watching from sidelines

dialogue.text: Even in play, he reshaped order; the chronicle notes revisions to Sagol Kangjei, the royal game on horseback that trained warriors as it delighted the court.

panels.shot: close-up on Khagemba’s thoughtful face as he speaks to a scribe with palm-leaf manuscript

dialogue.text: Parratt’s translation of the court chronicle shows a ruler attentive to rules, offices and rituals, tightening the cords that made Manipur a more ordered kingdom.

panels.shot: wide twilight shot of Kangla with gate, bridge, market lights and a mosque-like roofline in far background

dialogue.text: By the time Khagemba’s long reign ended in 1652, the valley held new bridges, coins, markets, and a settled Pangal community woven into its life.

panels.shot: slow push-in on an aged Khagemba in simple robes, holding a coin and looking towards the bridge

dialogue.text: His name, remembered as Khagemba, lives in chronicles and in the living memory of names, markets and roads that still follow the paths he traced.

panels.shot: concluding wide aerial shot over modern Imphal valley, faint overlay of older bridges and gates imagined beneath

dialogue.text: Khagemba’s story shows how a frontier king used captives, coins and clay to redraw his world—and how choices at the border can still echo in the names, bridges and markets of today.
